page: Amazon Web Services r8i-flex.xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor with 4 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz and includes 480 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 7 GHz, yielding 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or a GPU, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates strong single-core performance, with high marks in single-threaded gzip compression and single-threaded bzip3 decompression. However, multi-core scaling presents a notable tradeoff, as stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression fall into the lower 25% tier. Memory bandwidth tests show a similar divergence; while large block write speeds are average, read-only memory bandwidth for both small and large blocks is relatively weak.

The r8i-flex.xlarge offers a cost-efficient entry point for memory-intensive workloads that do not require continuous maximum multi-core CPU utilization. The high memory-to-vCPU ratio supports memory-bound tasks such as caching layers, Redis key-value stores, and light database operations, though complex database queries may be constrained by the lower multi-core performance. It is also suitable for single-threaded text processing, basic web serving, and small-scale language model inference.
